This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines--> [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kainan City)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines--> [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kainan City)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines--> [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kainan City)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines--> [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Kainan City)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

[[Category:qq-Kainan City)-qq]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
[[Category:qq-Kainan City)-->[[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
[[Category:qq deprecated open]]<!--Kainan City)-->[[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
[[Category:qq deprecated open]]<!--Kainan City)-->[[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
[[Category:qq deprecated open]]<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
[[Category:qq deprecated open]]<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.
== See Also == * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.
== See Also == * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}} - {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}} * {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)--> [[ja:九十九王子 (海南市)]] ==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
