==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|12=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|12=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|12=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|12=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|12=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|12=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|12=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|12=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|12=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|12=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)-->
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|12=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|12=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|12=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|12=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|12=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}} <!--subst:PAGENAME magic word should be substituted in the future when this is moved to its final pagename. This was added to a few pages not created on Feb 8 because they were very barren and this gives context to the fact that they are in a large group of pages all to be translated more or less as a group similar to the Ise Shrines-->
<!--Kainan City)-->
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|12=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|12=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|12=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|12=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|12=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|12=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|12=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|12=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|12=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|12=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.
== See Also == * {{ill|Kumano faith|ja|熊野信仰|1=Kumano Three Shrines|lt=Kumano faith|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}} - {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}} * {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūkuōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

revision.text:
本項目では、[[和歌山県]][[海南市]]内に所在する'''[[九十九王子]]'''（くじゅうくおうじ）について述べる。
== 九十九王子とは == ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[1221年]]（[[承久]]3年）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が和歌山県海南市内にある王子を扱う。
== 九十九王子 == 海南市内の九十九王子は9社。
=== 松坂王子 === [[File:松坂王子.jpg|thumb|松坂王子]] ''' 松坂王子'''（まつさかおうじ）跡地は、[[九十九王子 (和歌山市)#奈久知王子|奈久知王子]]から南下し、亀ノ川を渡って県道に突き当たる辺りにある。「熊野道之間愚記」（『[[明月記]]』所収）[[建仁]]元年（[[1201年]]）10月8日条に「次参松坂王子」とある。『[[民経記]]』[[承元]]4年（[[1210年]]）4月24 日条には「大野坂王子」<ref name="Kadokawa_1985_956">「角川日本地名大辞典」編纂委員会[1985: 956]</ref>、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]5年（[[1474年]]）の『王子記』では「小野坂王子」<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_64">長谷川[2007: 64]</ref>と記されるが、道順から松坂王子のことと推定されている<ref name="Kadokawa_1985_956"/>。[[寛文]]年間にはすでに近隣の八幡神社の末社の内に退転したとあり<ref>西[1987: 102]</ref>、現在地の庚申塚は、別のところから跡地に移されたものと伝えられる<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_64"/>。県指定史跡（[[1974年]]〈[[昭和]]49年〉4月9日指定）<ref name="Kinen">{{Cite web|和書 |publisher=和歌山県教育委員会 |url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkinen.html |title=県指定文化財・記念物 |accessdate=2009-04-09 }}</ref>。
* 所在地 - 海南市旦来1226-1
=== 松代王子 === [[File:松代王子跡.jpg|thumb|松代王子跡（春日神社）]] ''' 松代王子'''（まつしろおうじ）は、松坂王子から県道を南下して古道に入り、日方川沿いに進んで松代橋の傍らにある説明板と道標を手がかりに、山道に 200メートルほどわけ入ったところに緑泥片岩の石碑が建てられているあたりに比定される。「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月8日条、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月24日条に「松代」と記される<ref name="Kadokawa_1985_956"/>。この石碑は紀州藩の藩命で建てられたもので、表面に松代王子の刻字がある<ref>長谷川[2007: 66]</ref>。しかし、中世熊野参詣期の所在地は、社家をつとめた出口氏邸のあった春日山の西麓だったと伝えられる<ref>西[1987: 103]</ref>。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に春日神社（海南市大野中）に合祀された。県指定史跡（[[1958年]] 〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市大野中1055
=== 菩提房王子 === ''' 菩提房王子'''（ぼだいぼうおうじ）は、松代王子から古道に戻り、春日橋で日方川を越えて蓮花寺を過ぎた辺りにある。「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月8日条、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月24日条に「松代」と記される<ref>「角川日本地名大辞典」編纂委員会[1985: 944]</ref>。[[1942年]]（[[昭和]]17年）の『[[和歌山県聖蹟]]』では、4～5点の小さな石塔や石仏が置かれていると述べられている<ref>西[1987: 104]</ref>。江戸時代後期に紀州藩が編纂した地誌『[[紀伊続風土記]]』にこの王子についての廃跡との記述があり、早い時期に退転したものと見られる<ref>長谷川[2007: 67]</ref>。
* 所在地 - 海南市大野中95
=== 祓戸王子 === [[File:祓戸王子跡.jpg|thumb|祓戸王子跡]] ''' 祓戸王子'''（はらいどおうじ、はらえどおうじ）跡は、菩提房王子から西へ進み、[[紀勢本線]]の線路の手前を南に折れて、[[如来寺 (海南市)|如来寺]]裏手斜面にある墓地の中を通り、頂上を越したところに碑がある。街道からだいぶ離れた場所にあるが、かつてはもっと街道よりの麓近くにあったといわれ<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_68">長谷川[2007: 68]</ref><ref>西[1987: 105]</ref>、地元の伝承によれば如来寺の隣地であったという<ref name="Heibonsya_1997_682">平凡社[1997: 682]</ref>。[[1873年]]（明治6年）に村社に列格された当時は小さいながら社殿があり<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_68"/>、[[1873年]]（明治6年）付の記録によれば境内288坪とあるが、1909年（明治 42年）に藤白神社に合祀され、跡地には碑が建てられた<ref name="Heibonsya_1997_682"/>。
「熊野道之間愚記」の建仁元年（1201年）10月8日条には祓戸王子の名で記載が見られるが、藤原経光の参詣記（『民経記』所収）承元4年（1210年）4 月24日条には鳥居王子、[[仁和寺]]蔵の『熊野縁起』（[[正中 (日本)|正中]]3年〈[[1326年]]〉）には大鳥居王子と記されている。[[室町時代]]以降はもっぱら鳥居神社の名で呼ばれたと見られ、禅林寺文書や『紀伊続風土記』にも鳥居王子との言及がある<ref name="Heibonsya_1997_682"/>。
この辺りの地名を鳥居と称する。古くは熊野一ノ鳥居があった場所と考えられており、聖域に入る直前に身を清める潔斎所であったようだが、鳥居は[[天文 (元号)|天文]]18年（[[1549年]]）に失われたという<ref>長谷川[2007: 69]</ref>。[[熊野本宮大社]]のすぐ手前にある同名の王子（[[九十九王子 (田辺市本宮町)#祓戸王子|祓戸王子]]）も同様の役割を担っていた。今日では、[[藤白神社|藤白王子]]の二ノ鳥居の傍らに熊野一の鳥居と刻まれた石碑が設置され、祓戸王子を顕彰している。県指定史跡（1958年〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市鳥居257-1
=== 藤代王子 === [[ファイル:241006 Fujishiro-jinja Kainan Wakayama pref Japan30s3.jpg|thumb|藤代王子]] ''藤代王子（藤白王子）については[[藤白神社]]を参照''
=== 藤白塔下王子 === [[File:藤白塔下王子.jpg|thumb|藤白塔下王子]] ''' 藤白塔下王子'''（ふじしろとうげおうじ、藤白峠王子<ref name="Nishi_1987_107">西[1987: 107]</ref>とも）は、藤白神社の裏手の[[有間皇子]]の万葉歌碑から、藤白山に登る坂道（藤白坂）に取り付き、山頂にある無住寺、地蔵峰寺の境内に跡地がある。
藤白坂の路傍には町石がわりの丁石地蔵が祀られている。これらは江戸時代に海南の専念寺住持であった全長が建てたものと伝えられ、旅人の安全を祈念したものだという<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_73">長谷川[2007: 73]</ref>。境内には石碑があるが、遺物は遺されておらず竹薮があるばかりである。1909年（明治42年）に橘本王子神社に合祀されるまでは、若一王子神社と称され、祠もあったという<ref name="Nishi_1987_107"/><ref name="Hasegawa_2007_73"/>。地蔵峰寺の背後にある山頂には、御所ノ芝という展望所があり、そこからの眺望は『紀伊名所図会』や「熊野道之間愚記」にも絶景として讃えられている<ref name="Nishi_1987_107"/>。県指定史跡（1974年〈昭和49年〉4月9日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市下津町橘本1615
=== 橘本王子 === [[File:橘本王子跡.jpg|thumb|橘本王子跡（阿弥陀寺）]] '''橘本王子'''（きつもとおうじ）跡地へは、地蔵峰寺を後にし、ミカン畑の中を貫く古道をたどって道標に従って着く阿弥陀寺の境内にある。
阿弥陀寺の境内に橘本王子があったと伝えられるが、遺構らしきものは見られない。境内にはかつて橘の木があり、代々植え次がれてきたともいうが[[1940年]]前後に枯死したという<ref>西[1987: 108]</ref>。紛らわしいのだが、橘本王子と現在の橘本神社とは別の神社で、橘本王子は橘本神社に合祀されている<ref>長谷川[2007: 74]</ref>。県指定史跡（1974年〈昭和49年〉4月9日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市下津町橘本1084-2
=== 所坂王子 === ''所坂王子については[[橘本神社]]を参照''
=== 一壷王子 === [[File:一壷王子跡.jpg|thumb|一壷王子跡（川路王子神社）]] '''一壷王子'''（いちのつぼおうじ、いちつぼおうじ）は、市坪川沿いの古道をさらに南下したところにある山路王子神社の境内が旧址である。山路王子神社は秋の例大祭でおこなわれる奉納花相撲<ref>{{Cite web|和書 |publisher=海南市教育委員会 |url=http://www.city.kainan.wakayama.jp/icity/browser?ActionCode=content&ContentID=1140673744826&SiteID=0 |title=山路王子神社の奉納花相撲 |accessdate=2009-04-09 }}</ref>（「泣き相撲」とも。県無形民俗文化財、[[1974年]]〈昭和49年〉12月9日指定）<ref name="Kainan_Minzoku">{{Cite web|和書 |publisher=和歌山県教育委員会 |url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenminzoku.html |title=県指定文化財・民俗文化財 |accessdate=2009-04-09 }}</ref>や獅子舞<ref>{{Cite web|和書 |publisher=海南市教育委員会 |url=http://www.city.kainan.wakayama.jp/icity/browser?ActionCode=content&ContentID=1140672425431&SiteID=0 |title=山路王子神社の奉納獅子舞 |accessdate=2009-04-09 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書 |publisher=財団法人地域創造 |url=http://bunkashisan.ne.jp/search/ViewContent.php?from=11&ContentID=175 |title=和歌山県指定無形民俗文化財 山路王子神社の獅子舞 |accessdate=2009-12-19 }}</ref>（県指定無形民俗文化財、1974年〈昭和49年〉12月9日指定）<ref name="Kainan_Minzoku"/>で知られる。
かつて別当寺院として瑠璃山安養寺という寺院があったと伝えられ、その名残の鐘楼があるが、梵鐘は[[第二次世界大戦]]中の金属供出で失われたままである<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_75">長谷川[2007: 75]</ref>。[[結晶片岩|緑泥片岩]]の石垣を4段に積み上げた中央に階段があり、最上部に社殿があり、先の[[橘本神社]]と似ている<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_75"/>。県指定史跡（1958年〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市下津町市坪269

revision.text:
本項目では、[[和歌山県]][[海南市]]内に所在する'''[[九十九王子]]'''（くじゅうくおうじ）について述べる。
== 九十九王子とは == ''詳細は[[九十九王子]]を参照''
九十九王子（くじゅうくおうじ）とは、[[熊野古道]]、特に[[紀伊路]]沿いに在する[[神社]]のうち、主に[[12世紀]]から[[13世紀]]にかけて、皇族・貴人の熊野詣に際して先達をつとめた熊野修験の手で急速に組織された一群の神社をいい、参詣者の守護が祈願された。
しかしながら、[[1221年]]（[[承久]]3年）の[[承久の乱]]以降、[[京都|京]]からの熊野詣が下火になり、そのルートであった紀伊路が衰退するとともに、荒廃と退転がすすんだ。[[室町時代]]以降、熊野詣がかつてのような卓越した地位を失うにつれ、この傾向はいっそう進み、[[江戸時代|近世]][[紀州藩]]の手による顕彰も行なわれたものの、勢いをとどめるまでには至らなかった。さらに、[[明治]]以降の[[神道]]の[[国家神道]]化とそれに伴う合祀、市街化による廃絶などにより、旧社地が失われたり、比定地が不明になったものも多い。
本記事では、これら九十九王子のうち、比定地が和歌山県海南市内にある王子を扱う。
== 九十九王子 == 海南市内の九十九王子は9社。
=== 松坂王子 === [[File:松坂王子.jpg|thumb|松坂王子]] ''' 松坂王子'''（まつさかおうじ）跡地は、[[九十九王子 (和歌山市)#奈久知王子|奈久知王子]]から南下し、亀ノ川を渡って県道に突き当たる辺りにある。「熊野道之間愚記」（『[[明月記]]』所収）[[建仁]]元年（[[1201年]]）10月8日条に「次参松坂王子」とある。『[[民経記]]』[[承元]]4年（[[1210年]]）4月24 日条には「大野坂王子」<ref name="Kadokawa_1985_956">「角川日本地名大辞典」編纂委員会[1985: 956]</ref>、[[文明 (日本)|文明]]5年（[[1474年]]）の『王子記』では「小野坂王子」<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_64">長谷川[2007: 64]</ref>と記されるが、道順から松坂王子のことと推定されている<ref name="Kadokawa_1985_956"/>。[[寛文]]年間にはすでに近隣の八幡神社の末社の内に退転したとあり<ref>西[1987: 102]</ref>、現在地の庚申塚は、別のところから跡地に移されたものと伝えられる<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_64"/>。県指定史跡（[[1974年]]〈[[昭和]]49年〉4月9日指定）<ref name="Kinen">{{Cite web|和書 |publisher=和歌山県教育委員会 |url=http://www.pref.wakayama.lg.jp/prefg/500700/mokuroku/mokuroku/kenkinen.html |title=県指定文化財・記念物 |accessdate=2009-04-09 }}</ref>。
* 所在地 - 海南市旦来1226-1
=== 松代王子 === [[File:松代王子跡.jpg|thumb|松代王子跡（春日神社）]] ''' 松代王子'''（まつしろおうじ）は、松坂王子から県道を南下して古道に入り、日方川沿いに進んで松代橋の傍らにある説明板と道標を手がかりに、山道に 200メートルほどわけ入ったところに緑泥片岩の石碑が建てられているあたりに比定される。「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月8日条、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月24日条に「松代」と記される<ref name="Kadokawa_1985_956"/>。この石碑は紀州藩の藩命で建てられたもので、表面に松代王子の刻字がある<ref>長谷川[2007: 66]</ref>。しかし、中世熊野参詣期の所在地は、社家をつとめた出口氏邸のあった春日山の西麓だったと伝えられる<ref>西[1987: 103]</ref>。[[1909年]]（[[明治]]42年）に春日神社（海南市大野中）に合祀された。県指定史跡（[[1958年]] 〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市大野中1055
=== 菩提房王子 === ''' 菩提房王子'''（ぼだいぼうおうじ）は、松代王子から古道に戻り、春日橋で日方川を越えて蓮花寺を過ぎた辺りにある。「熊野道之間愚記」建仁元年（1201年）10月8日条、『民経記』承元4年（1210年）4月24日条に「松代」と記される<ref>「角川日本地名大辞典」編纂委員会[1985: 944]</ref>。[[1942年]]（[[昭和]]17年）の『[[和歌山県聖蹟]]』では、4～5点の小さな石塔や石仏が置かれていると述べられている<ref>西[1987: 104]</ref>。江戸時代後期に紀州藩が編纂した地誌『[[紀伊続風土記]]』にこの王子についての廃跡との記述があり、早い時期に退転したものと見られる<ref>長谷川[2007: 67]</ref>。
* 所在地 - 海南市大野中95
=== 祓戸王子 === [[File:祓戸王子跡.jpg|thumb|祓戸王子跡]] ''' 祓戸王子'''（はらいどおうじ、はらえどおうじ）跡は、菩提房王子から西へ進み、[[紀勢本線]]の線路の手前を南に折れて、[[如来寺 (海南市)|如来寺]]裏手斜面にある墓地の中を通り、頂上を越したところに碑がある。街道からだいぶ離れた場所にあるが、かつてはもっと街道よりの麓近くにあったといわれ<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_68">長谷川[2007: 68]</ref><ref>西[1987: 105]</ref>、地元の伝承によれば如来寺の隣地であったという<ref name="Heibonsya_1997_682">平凡社[1997: 682]</ref>。[[1873年]]（明治6年）に村社に列格された当時は小さいながら社殿があり<ref name="Hasegawa_2007_68"/>、[[1873年]]（明治6年）付の記録によれば境内288坪とあるが、1909年（明治 42年）に藤白神社に合祀され、跡地には碑が建てられた<ref name="Heibonsya_1997_682"/>。
「熊野道之間愚記」の建仁元年（1201年）10月8日条には祓戸王子の名で記載が見られるが、藤原経光の参詣記（『民経記』所収）承元4年（1210年）4 月24日条には鳥居王子、[[仁和寺]]蔵の『熊野縁起』（[[正中 (日本)|正中]]3年〈[[1326年]]〉）には大鳥居王子と記されている。[[室町時代]]以降はもっぱら鳥居神社の名で呼ばれたと見られ、禅林寺文書や『紀伊続風土記』にも鳥居王子との言及がある<ref name="Heibonsya_1997_682"/>。
この辺りの地名を鳥居と称する。古くは熊野一ノ鳥居があった場所と考えられており、聖域に入る直前に身を清める潔斎所であったようだが、鳥居は[[天文 (元号)|天文]]18年（[[1549年]]）に失われたという<ref>長谷川[2007: 69]</ref>。[[熊野本宮大社]]のすぐ手前にある同名の王子（[[九十九王子 (田辺市本宮町)#祓戸王子|祓戸王子]]）も同様の役割を担っていた。今日では、[[藤白神社|藤白王子]]の二ノ鳥居の傍らに熊野一の鳥居と刻まれた石碑が設置され、祓戸王子を顕彰している。県指定史跡（1958年〈昭和33年〉4月1日指定）<ref name="Kinen"/>。
* 所在地 - 海南市鳥居257-1
=== 藤代王子 === [[ファイル:241006 Fujishiro-jinja Kainan Wakayama pref Japan30s3.jpg|thumb|藤代王子]] ''藤代王子（藤白王子）については[[藤白神社]]を参照''

=== 橘本王子 === [[File:橘本王子跡.jpg|thumb|橘本王子跡（阿弥陀寺）]] '''橘本王子'''（きつもとおうじ）跡地へは、地蔵峰寺を後にし、ミカン畑の中を貫く古道をたどって道標に従って着く阿弥陀寺の境内にある。

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|12=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|12=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|12=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|12=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|12=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|12=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|12=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|12=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|12=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|12=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|12=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|12=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|12=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|12=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|12=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|12=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|12=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|12=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|12=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|12=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|12=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|12=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|12=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|qq=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|qq=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|qq=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|qq=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|qq=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|qq=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|qq=draft}}
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|1=Kujūku Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|qq=draft}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of {{ill|shrines|ja|神社|qq=draft}} located along the {{ill|Kumano Kodo|ja|熊野古道|1=Kumano Kodō|qq=draft}}, particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the {{ill|Jokyu Rebellion|ja|承久の乱|qq=draft}} in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the {{ill|Muromachi period|ja|室町時代|qq=draft}}, as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the {{ill|Kishu Domain|ja|紀州藩|qq=draft}} during the {{ill|Edo period|ja|江戸時代|qq=draft}} to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft}} and the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|ja|国家神道|qq=draft}} led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in {{ill|Kainan City|ja|海南市|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|ja|和歌山県|qq=draft}}.
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
