revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Kujuku Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Kujuku Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Kujuku Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Kujuku Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Kujuku Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Kujuku Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujūku Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
== References == * Hasegawa, Yasutaka (2007). *Kumano Ōji Pilgrimage Guidebook*. Shinpu Shobo. * Heibonsha (1997). *Great Dictionary of Temples and Shrines in Yamato and Kii*. Heibonsha. * Nishi, Ritsu (1987). *Kumano Kodo Michishirube*. Arawasei Bundō.

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

revision.text:
This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269

This is a list of some of the {{ill|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|fr|Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=99 ōji Shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}} on the [[Kumano Kodō]]. This article covers the ōji Shrines in the region of [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]]
==Overview== '''Ninety-Nine Ōji (九十九王子) in Kainan City'''
== What is Ninety-Nine Ōji? == ''For more details, see {{ill|Kujuku Oji|ja|九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|2=ja|3=九十九王子|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|4=fr|5=Kujūkuōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|1=Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujuku Oji|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninety-Nine Ōji|lt=Ninety-Nine Ōji|qq=}}.''
The term '''Ninety-Nine Ōji''' (九十九王子) refers to a group of [[:en:Shinto shrine|shrines]] located along the [[:en:Kumano Kodō|Kumano Kodō]], particularly the {{ill|Kiiji Route|ja|紀伊路|1=Kiiji|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji Route|13=User:Immanuelle/Kiiji|qq=}}. These shrines were rapidly organized primarily between the 12th and 13th centuries by practitioners of {{ill|Kumano Shugendo|ja|熊野修験|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Shugendo|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} to serve as protective deities for imperial family members and nobility making pilgrimages to Kumano.
However, after the [[:en:Jōkyū War|Jokyu Rebellion]] in 1221, pilgrimages from {{ill|Kyoto|ja|京都|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto|qq=}} dwindled, and the Kiiji Route declined, leading to the deterioration and abandonment of many of these shrines. This trend continued after the [[:en:Muromachi period|Muromachi period]], as Kumano pilgrimages lost their former prominence. Despite efforts by the [[:en:Kishū Domain|Kishu Domain]] during the [[:en:Edo period|Edo period]] to honor these shrines, they never regained their former vitality. The [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]] and the establishment of [[:en:State Shinto|State Shinto]] led to further shrine mergers and urban development, causing many original sites to be lost or unidentified.
This article focuses on the Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines located in [[:en:Kainan, Wakayama|Kainan City]], [[:en:Wakayama Prefecture|Wakayama Prefecture]].
== Ninety-Nine Ōji Shrines in Kainan City == There are nine Ninety-Nine Ōji shrines identified within Kainan City.
=== Matsuzaka Ōji === [[File:Matsuzaka_Oji.jpg|thumb|Matsuzaka Ōji]] The site of '''Matsuzaka Ōji''' (松坂王子) is located south of {{ill|Nakuchi Oji|ja|奈久知王子|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nakuchi Oji|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, near the crossing of the Kamegawa River. It is mentioned in the "{{ill|Kumano Michi no Maguki|ja|熊野道之間愚記|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Michi no Maguki|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}" (1201) and other records under different names such as "Onozaka Ōji." The site was later integrated as a subsidiary shrine of the local {{ill|Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman shrine|lt=Hachiman Shrine|ja|八幡神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 八幡宮}}. It has been designated as a prefectural historic site since 1974.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Danki 1226-1
=== Matsushiro Ōji === [[File:Matsushiro_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Matsushiro Ōji Site (Kasuga Shrine)]] '''Matsushiro Ōji''' (松代王子) is identified near the Matsushiro Bridge, along the old pilgrimage route. A commemorative stone monument was erected by the Kishu Domain. In 1909, it was merged into {{ill|Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|ja|春日神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrine (Kainan|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 1055
=== Bodaibo Ōji === '''Bodaibo Ōji''' (菩提房王子) is located past the Renkeiji Temple. Small stone statues and remnants mark the site. The shrine was already in decline by the Edo period.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Onochu 95
=== Haraido Ōji === [[File:Haraido_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Haraido Ōji Site]] The site of '''Haraido Ōji''' (祓戸王子) is near {{ill|Nyorai-ji Temple|ja|如来寺|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nyorai-ji Temple|qq=}}. It was previously known as "Torii Ōji" in historical records. A commemorative stone now marks the site.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Torii 257-1
=== Fujishiro Ōji === For details on '''Fujishiro Ōji''' (藤代王子), see {{ill|Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Ōji|lt=Fujishiro Shrine|ja|藤白神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujishiro Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Fujishiro Toge Ōji === [[File:Fujishiro_Toge_Oji.jpg|thumb|Fujishiro Toge Ōji]] '''Fujishiro Toge Ōji''' (藤白塔下王子) is located along the Fujishiro Pass. A stone monument marks the site. It was merged with {{ill|Tachibana Oji Shrine|ja|橘本王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Oji Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in 1909.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1615
=== Tachibana Ōji === [[File:Tachibana_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Tachibana Ōji Site (Amida Temple)]] The site of '''Tachibana Ōji''' (橘本王子) is located within the grounds of Amida Temple. It is separate from the current {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Tachibana 1084-2
=== Tokorozaka Ōji === For details on '''Tokorozaka Ōji''' (所坂王子), see {{ill|Tachibana Shrine|ja|橘本神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tachibana Shrine|qq=}}.
=== Ichinotsubo Ōji === [[File:Ichinotsubo_Oji_site.jpg|thumb|Ichinotsubo Ōji Site (Kawaji Ōji Shrine)]] The site of '''Ichinotsubo Ōji''' (一壷王子) is within the grounds of {{ill|Yamaji Oji Shrine|ja|山路王子神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yamaji Oji Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, known for its traditional "Crying Sumo" festival, designated as an intangible cultural property.
* '''Location:''' Kainan City, Shimotsu Town, Ichitsubo 269
